selected.rationale: The Fitness Enthusiast works out 4+ times a week and actively buys supplements, matching the core workout supplements, creatine, and protein offering of this advertiser. Their price sensitivity is low-medium, meaning they appreciate the high-performance formulations while being highly receptive to the advertiser's value proposition of getting the same results for half the cost.

The Wellness Optimizer tracks supplements and workouts as part of a systematic approach to health. They align well with the advertiser's wellness_dtc category and will respond strongly to ingredient transparency, matching the scientific integrity needed to trust a budget-friendly alternative to expensive supplement brands.

The Value-Conscious Shopper is budget-aware, reads reviews, and comparison shops. This directly corresponds to the advertiser's competitive strategy of competing on price and providing the exact same formulations as expensive brands for half the cost.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent focuses on meal kits, household items, and kids products rather than workout supplements, and their affinity for subscriptions conflicts with the advertiser's one-off business model.

The Gen Z Aesthete focuses on beauty, fashion, and visual brand identity discovered through TikTok, whereas this advertiser competes strictly on price and formulation functionality rather than aesthetic-forward lifestyle branding.
The Pet Parent focuses entirely on pet food, pet supplies, and pet health, which has no overlap with human workout supplements.
The Affluent Classic has an age range of 50-68 and focuses on luxury home goods and classic apparel, completely missing the 18-45 age demographic and wellness focus of this advertiser.

The Sustainability Buyer focuses on environmental footprint, supply chain transparency, and sustainable apparel, whereas the advertiser's brief centres strictly on athletic formulation equivalence and price competition rather than eco-friendly positioning.
The Convenience-First Millennial relies heavily on instant delivery and subscription services, which contradicts the advertiser's one-off purchase business model and focus on raw product pricing.

The Gifter buys for others during holidays and special events with a focus on premium presentation and gift-wrapping, which is fundamentally misaligned with self-use routine workout supplements bought for functional value.
